text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croatia proposes a meeting between President Franjo Tudjman and Bosnia's Alija Izetbegovic within the next 10 days after it was postponed for a third time.
- A showdown between head of the Social Liberals (HSLS) Vlado Gotovac and his main rival within the party Drazen Budisa has created a definite rift between their two factions.
- Six people have been detained in Zadar for illegally selling houses abandoned by Serbs during the war.
- State bank HBOR tops the list of the most succesful banks in 1996 according to equity capital. Zagrebacka Banka ranks first when it comes to assets and profit.
- A proposed law on investment funds sets the minimum equity at 12.5 million for funds to take care of mass privatisation shares.

- Fifteen out of 20 registered insurers in Croatia increased their premium income 10 percent to 3.1 billion kuna in 1996. Croatia Osiguranje remained at the helm with a 71.4 percent market share, down from 77.1 percent in 1995.

- Following the arrest of Slavko Dokmanovic by the U.N. war crimes tribunal and the U.N. in Eastern Slavonia: Witnesses claim he beat three people to death on Ovcara and he commanded the torture of other Croatian soldiers in Vukovar.

- State oil firm INA has a surplus of 5,000-7,000 workers. Nobody will be made redundant at the moment, but those who wish to leave will be given a 100,000 kuna loan. They have to guarantee they would not register as unemployed for two years.
- In the past few years, the Catholic church has imposed stricter criteria for those wishing a church wedding. Bride and groom must now have some of the more important sacraments.
- Tourist results show this summer season will be better than expected, says Tourism Minister Niko Bulic. In 1998 Croatia can expect 30 million overnights, or a further 20 percent rise.
- Croatian and Italian joint search for oil in the Adriatic sea: in the first three-year phase joint oil firm INAgip will do all seizmic tests and draw a map on quantities of resources.

- "I lost from the guy who kept falling on the ground. He is a good player, but not on grass. My returns were disastrous. Terrible, terrible," says Goran Ivanisevic who lost against Swede Magnus Norman 3:6, 6:2, 6:7, 6:4, 12:14 in Wimbledon.
- Fire devastated 200 hectares of forest and brush near Dubrovnik. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
